system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Cole Credit Property Trust III, Inc. realized record (fixed ~2016–2018 window)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is fixed at approximately three to
> five years after the ~2013 closing (approximately 2016–2018). This sub-dossier contains no
> information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Realized completion of the closing-era transaction (2013)
- The manager-internalization merger was completed effective April 5, 2013: Holdings merged
  into the registrant's wholly owned subsidiary (Merger Sub), and the selling executives
  received a total of $20.0 million in cash (subject to adjustment) and 10,711,225
  newly-issued shares of the registrant's common stock. [SRC: SEC accession 0001425923-13-000006, Form 8-K dated April 5, 2013]
- Leadership changed at completion: on April 5, 2013 Christopher H. Cole resigned as chief
  executive officer and president and the board appointed Marc T. Nemer to those positions;
  Cole remained a director and became executive chairman. [SRC: SEC accession 0001425923-13-000006, Form 8-K dated April 5, 2013]
- On April 11, 2013 the registrant issued a press release commenting that American Realty
  Capital Properties, Inc. had withdrawn its earlier unsolicited proposal to acquire 100% of
  the registrant's outstanding common stock. [SRC: SEC accession 0001425923-13-000006, Form 8-K dated April 5, 2013]

## Acquisition and end of independent public existence (2013–2014)
- The registrant subsequently listed its common stock on the New York Stock Exchange under
  the name Cole Real Estate Investments, Inc. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-040724, Form 8-K dated February 7, 2014]
- On October 22, 2013 Cole Real Estate Investments, Inc. entered into an Agreement and Plan
  of Merger with American Realty Capital Properties, Inc. and Clark Acquisition, LLC. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-040724, Form 8-K dated February 7, 2014]
- The merger was consummated on February 7, 2014: each outstanding share of Cole common
  stock (other than shares held by ARCP or affiliates) converted into the right to receive
  either 1.0929 shares of ARCP common stock or $13.82 in cash; the shares of Cole common
  stock were delisted and removed from trading on the NYSE prior to the open of trading on
  February 7, 2014. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-040724, Form 8-K dated February 7, 2014]
- Registration of the entity was terminated: a Form 15 filed February 18, 2014 by "ARC
  Properties Operating Partnership, L.P., successor to Clark Acquisition, LLC, successor to
  Cole Real Estate Investments, Inc." certified termination of registration under the
  Exchange Act, reporting an approximate number of holders of record as of the notice date
  of "One"; it was signed by Nicholas S. Schorsch. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-14-010247, Form 15-12B filed February 18, 2014]

## Availability of a record within the fixed outcome window (~2016–2018)
- The registrant's last annual report on Form 10-K was the one for fiscal year 2012; no
  Form 10-K or 20-F was filed by this registrant for any later fiscal year, and its EDGAR
  filing history ends with the February 2014 acquisition filings and the Form 15
  deregistration. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-14-010247, Form 15-12B filed February 18, 2014]
- Because the entity was acquired by American Realty Capital Properties and deregistered in
  February 2014, no separate audited public financial statements or annual reports exist for
  this entity for the fixed ~2016–2018 outcome window; the acquirer did not, in a source
  retrieved here, separately disclose the former portfolio's standalone post-acquisition
  trajectory. Any outcome scalar for that window is therefore not primary-verifiable for this
  entity. [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-14-010247, Form 15-12B filed February 18, 2014]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- No standalone segment disclosure of the acquired portfolio's ~2016–2018 realized results
  was located for this entity; the acquirer's consolidated results are not used to infer an
  outcome for this entity. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The manager-internalization merger completed in April 2013 with a leadership change, and
  within about ten months the entity was itself acquired: it listed on the NYSE as Cole Real
  Estate Investments, Inc., agreed on October 22, 2013 to be acquired by American Realty
  Capital Properties, completed that merger on February 7, 2014 ($13.82 cash or 1.0929 ARCP
  shares per Cole share; NYSE delisting), and terminated its Exchange Act registration on
  February 18, 2014 with a single holder of record. Consequently there is no separate public
  audited record for this entity within the fixed ~2016–2018 outcome window, and the outcome
  for that window is coded uncertain (no separate public record). [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-14-040724, Form 8-K dated February 7, 2014] [SRC: SEC accession 0001144204-14-010247, Form 15-12B filed February 18, 2014]

[SLICE END]
